summary: THE RE-ENGAGEMENT LASTED EXACTLY ONE WEEK. Last week's report led with the best news this account had produced in a month: after 35 days of saying nothing, Sarah started asking us for things again — four real asks in seven days, 26 messages, six different ALTR people talking to her. The state file's explicit warning was that three of those four asks got non-answers and that 'if this window's asks go the way the previous ones did, expect her to stop again.' She stopped again. In the seven days to Sep 25 Sarah asked ALTR for NOTHING. Not one question, not one request, not one chase. Her fifteen messages are two things: an apology for a late payment, and a batch of creator tags WE asked her for. ALTR'S ENTIRE WRITTEN OUTPUT THIS WEEK WAS THREE MESSAGES AND ABOUT TWENTY-SIX WORDS, FROM TWO PEOPLE. In full: Olivia on Sep 18 — 'Hi Sarah & team, could someone provide me with the creator tags for the b/g and g/g content'; Stephski on Sep 21 — 'all good! Thanks so much 🙂'; Olivia on Sep 23 — 'tysm for these!'. That is it. Six ALTR people posted last week; two posted this week, and neither of them advanced a single ALTR deliverable. One of the three messages was us asking HER for something. The other two were thank-yous. Mayson Chat — the de facto account manager, 13 of 32 ALTR messages last week, the only person on this account who reliably starts conversations — went silent for the first time in weeks and is now 8 days quiet. Vivek, who owns all three of her dead Instagram accounts, is 11 days quiet. Derrek is 7 days quiet and his last words to this client remain 'damn OF Is on their shit'. SHE PAID, AND THAT IS THE ONLY THING THAT MOVED. The Sep 1-14 invoice, issued Sep 15, was settled at 03:54 on Sep 20 — four days and fourteen hours, against an 18-hour turnaround on the previous cycle, after two chases from Stephski and after she apologised twice. On Sep 18 she wrote 'Hey Steph!! I’m so sorry I have not forgotten about this!! My bank is being stupid atm, I promise I’ll transfer in the next few hours!' and then took a further thirty hours. She blamed her own bank, not our contradictory instructions — which is characteristic and does not mean we are off the hook. Stephski acknowledged 36 hours later with five words and never said which account received it, never explained the Sep 15 contradiction, never apologised for it, and never pinned corrected details. The 1:1 banking confirmation call recommended as the top action last week did not happen. Ten days on, the sixth change of payment instructions in twelve months is still unreconciled on the record. IT WAS A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SINGLE TRANSFER. For eleven months every invoice was split into two halves because her bank caps international transfers at 50k AUD/day. Aug 25, Sep 2 and now Sep 20 were all one payment. Three data points is confirmation, not noise: her invoices — and therefore her net earnings — have roughly halved. That is consistent with 'about 17.5' on Aug 22, with her own 'why have I gone down to 3k days' on Aug 8, and with her ~530k-follower main Instagram being dead since Aug 9. Nobody at ALTR has pulled the actual Jul-Aug net figures in the 28 days since Derrek was asked to. We are watching our own revenue halve inside our own billing system and nobody has looked. THE DMCA SERVICE IS NOW DEAD. Michelle Queue's weekly leak-removal breakdown ran seven straight weeks — Jul 26, Aug 1, Aug 10, Aug 17, Aug 25, Sep 1, Sep 8 — and has now missed two consecutive weeks. Last post 17 days ago, no message of any kind, no explanation. Last week's report set the test explicitly: 'if it misses a second week the DMCA service is effectively dead on this account.' It missed. Meanwhile the ~20 leak URLs she hand-collected on Jul 18 at Michelle's own invitation are 69 days old, answered once with 'their being worked on babes 💕' and only after an internal tag. FOURTH CONSECUTIVE REPORTING PERIOD WITH ZERO CARRIED COMMITMENTS CLOSED. Every single item aged another week: @sarah.h44 47 days with still not one written sentence from ALTR about its status; @onlysarahh_xx and @sarah.hxx 50 days and unmentioned by anybody for a second straight week; the earnings plan 48 days with its owner now 42 days absent; Derrek's Phone Farm updates 55 days; the Jul 18 leak links 69 days; the AI voice clone 27 days; the Sep 2 OFTV call write-up 23 days; the Sep 5 trial-reels write-up 20 days; the Snapchat scope 16 days; Facebook 9 days; the Sep 18 chargeback 7 days and never answered by anyone; credentials-out-of-the-group-chat 35 days and still sitting in scrollback. THE ONE THING SHE DID DO SHE DID PERFECTLY, AS ALWAYS. Olivia asked for creator tags on Sep 17 and again on Sep 18; Sarah delivered eleven tagged screenshots on Sep 19 and then volunteered something nobody asked for — 'Also the guy in my vids is in the release form section under Justin' — pre-empting the model-release compliance question on her b/g content. Olivia thanked her four days later. That is the whole relationship in miniature: she over-delivers on everything we ask, we take four days to say thanks, and nothing she is actually paying 30% of net for gets touched. THE CHURN PICTURE. She has not been slow to us in twelve months, she still signs off with 'Thanks heaps x', and she paid. But: zero asks, no message at all since 03:56 on Sep 20 (five days at window close), a payment that took 4.5 days instead of 18 hours, billings confirmed halved, her main distribution asset dead for seven weeks with no written status, and an agency whose entire weekly contribution was 26 words. A client on a month-to-month 30% agreement who has stopped asking her agency for anything is not being difficult. She is doing the arithmetic.

health.rationale: Down 11 from 48 on 2026-09-18, and this is the lowest score this account has ever recorded — below the 38 of Aug 21, the week that had one message in it. That needs justifying, because this week she paid her invoice and answered a request, and Aug 21 was a corpse. The justification is that Aug 21 was a risk and this week is a result. Last week ALTR ran an accidental experiment: six people started conversations with her and she responded with four real asks and 26 messages, the first time she had asked for anything in five weeks. Three of those four asks were answered with nine words, a 4.5-hour-late reply and a five-word joke. This week she asked for nothing at all. The experiment ran, ALTR failed it, and the client's behaviour reverted inside seven days — which converts 'she has gone quiet' from a worry into evidence about what happens when she doesn't. The next restart will be harder than this one was, and there may not be a third. Against that: ALTR's total output was three messages and roughly 26 words from two people, one of which was a request TO her. Mayson, the only functioning account manager, went silent for the first time in weeks (8 days). Vivek (11 days) owns three dead Instagram accounts including a ~530k main that is now 47 days down with zero written status across seven consecutive reporting windows. Michelle's weekly DMCA breakdown missed a second consecutive week after seven unbroken ones — last week's stated test for whether the service is dead, now failed, with hand-submitted links at 69 days. Zero carried commitments closed for a FOURTH consecutive period; every item simply aged. The Sep 18 chargeback she flagged was never answered by anyone. The banking contradiction of Sep 15 was never reconciled, never apologised for, never pinned — the recommended 1:1 call did not happen — and Stephski's receipt confirmation was five words that did not say which account the money landed in. The two genuine positives are real but small and both are hers, not ours: she paid, and she delivered the tags plus an unprompted release-form note. And the payment itself carries the worst structural signal on the account — a third consecutive single transfer, confirming at three data points that her invoices have fallen below her 50k AUD/day bank cap, i.e. her earnings have roughly halved, while the request to pull the actual net figures sits 28 days old and untouched. We are collecting a shrinking fee from a client whose main growth asset we have not spoken about in seven weeks.

Vivek has been silent for 11 days. She has raised it herself at least six times (2026-08-07, 08-08, 08-09, 08-31, 09-01, 09-13) and last week she re-opened it personally, handed over her login in plaintext, got nine words back and watched the thread vanish into a DM with no record.
